facts.fact_text: The applicant party, the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP), is a parliamentary political party in the Republic of Moldova.
The Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) was in opposition at the time of the events described in the case.

On 26 December 2001, the parliamentary group of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) informed Chișinău Municipal Council of its intention to hold a meeting with its supporters on 9 January 2002.
The meeting planned by the CDPP parliamentary group for 9 January 2002 was to be held in Great National Assembly Square, in front of the government buildings.
The CDPP parliamentary group stated that the meeting planned for 9 January 2002 would relate to the introduction of the compulsory study of Russian in schools.
On 9 January 2002, the parliamentary group of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) held a gathering in Great National Assembly Square, in front of government headquarters.
The parliamentary group of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) also held gatherings on 11, 13, 15, 16 and 17 January 2002.
The Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) did not seek authorisation in accordance with the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 for the gatherings held in January 2002.

By a decision of 3 January 2002, Chișinău Municipal Council classified the gathering to be held on 9 January 2002 as a 'demonstration' within the meaning of sections 4, 8, 12 and 13 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995.

By a decision of 3 January 2002, Chișinău Municipal Council authorised the parliamentary group of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) to hold the gathering on 9 January 2002 in National Opera Square rather than Great National Assembly Square.

In its warning of 14 January 2002, the Ministry of Justice stated that the CDPP had breached the provisions of section 6 of the Assemblies Act by organising demonstrations in Great National Assembly Square on 9, 10, 11 and 13 January 2002.

In its warning of 14 January 2002, the Ministry of Justice stated that the CDPP had organised demonstrations in Great National Assembly Square notwithstanding that the authorisation issued by Chișinău Municipal Council only gave permission for a demonstration on 9 January 2002 in National Opera Square.
In its warning of 14 January 2002, the Ministry of Justice called for an immediate halt to the gatherings, which it considered to be illegal and unconstitutional.

In its warning of 14 January 2002, the Ministry of Justice warned the CDPP that if it failed to comply with the warning, the Ministry would impose a temporary ban (suspendarea activităţii) on the party's activities in accordance with section 29 of the Parties and other Socio-Political Organisations Act.

On 18 January 2002, the Ministry of Justice issued a decision imposing a one-month ban on the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP)'s activities, in accordance with section 29 of the Parties and other Socio-Political Organisations Act of 17 September 1991.
The one-month ban on the CDPP's activities imposed on 18 January 2002 was based on the organisation by the CDPP of unauthorised demonstrations on 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, 16 and 17 January 2002.
On 25 February 2002, the Supreme Court of Justice ruled in favour of the government and declared the CDPP gatherings illegal.

By a decision of 3 January 2002, Chișinău Municipal Council classified the gathering to be held on 9 January 2002 as a 'demonstration' within the meaning of sections 4, 8, 12 and 13 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995.

By a decision of 3 January 2002, Chișinău Municipal Council authorised the parliamentary group of the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP) to hold the gathering on 9 January 2002 in National Opera Square rather than Great National Assembly Square.

In its warning of 14 January 2002, the Ministry of Justice stated that the CDPP had breached the provisions of section 6 of the Assemblies Act by organising demonstrations in Great National Assembly Square on 9, 10, 11 and 13 January 2002.

In its warning of 14 January 2002, the Ministry of Justice stated that the CDPP had organised demonstrations in Great National Assembly Square notwithstanding that the authorisation issued by Chișinău Municipal Council only gave permission for a demonstration on 9 January 2002 in National Opera Square.

In its warning of 14 January 2002, the Ministry of Justice warned the CDPP that if it failed to comply with the warning, the Ministry would impose a temporary ban (suspendarea activităţii) on the party's activities in accordance with section 29 of the Parties and other Socio-Political Organisations Act.

On 18 January 2002, the Ministry of Justice issued a decision imposing a one-month ban on the Christian Democratic People's Party (CDPP)'s activities, in accordance with section 29 of the Parties and other Socio-Political Organisations Act of 17 September 1991.

According to the Ministry of Justice's decision of 18 January 2002, the CDPP had breached the provisions of sections 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11 of the Assemblies Act by not obtaining prior authorisation from Chișinău Municipal Council to stage demonstrations.
According to the Ministry of Justice's decision of 18 January 2002, the CDPP had breached the provisions of sections 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11 of the Assemblies Act by blocking the public highway.

Section 6(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be conducted peacefully, without any sort of weapons, and shall ensure the protection of participants and the environment, without impeding the normal use of public highways, road traffic and the operation of economic undertakings and without degenerating into acts of violence capable of endangering the public order and the physical integrity and life of persons or their property.

Section 8(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies may be conducted in squares, streets, parks and other public places in cities, towns and villages, and also in public buildings.

Section 8(3)(a) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within fifty metres of the parliament building, the residence of the President of Moldova, the seat of the government, the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court of Justice.

Article 15(2) of the International Convention on the Rights of the Child of 20 November 1989 provides that no restrictions may be placed on the exercise of children's rights to freedom of association and peaceful assembly other than those imposed in conformity with the law and which are necessary in a democratic society in the interests of national security or public safety, public order (ordre public), the protection of public health or morals or the protection of the rights and freedoms of others.
Chișinău Municipal Council's decision of 3 January 2002 did not give any reasons for the change of location from Great National Assembly Square to National Opera Square.

On 23 January 2002, Chișinău Municipal Council addressed a letter to the Ministry of Justice informing it that there was a discrepancy between the provisions of the Status of Members of Parliament Act and those of the Assemblies Act.

In its letter of 23 January 2002, Chișinău Municipal Council informed the Ministry of Justice that it did not know which of the two Acts — the Status of Members of Parliament Act or the Assemblies Act — to apply.

In its letter of 23 January 2002, Chișinău Municipal Council stated that a number of reputable lawyers supported the idea that CDPP members of parliament had the right to hold meetings with their supporters in Great National Assembly Square without obtaining prior authorisation, in accordance with sections 22 and 23 of the Status of Members of Parliament Act.

In its letter of 23 January 2002, Chișinău Municipal Council cited the opinion of an ombudsman who considered that, since section 23 of the Status of Members of Parliament Act proclaimed the right of members of parliament to raise demands on the spot for action to remedy a breach of the law, the CDPP members of parliament were entitled to raise their demands for the cessation of the alleged breaches concerning the introduction of compulsory Russian lessons in front of the government building.
In its letter of 23 January 2002, Chișinău Municipal Council requested the Ministry of Justice to ask Parliament for an official interpretation of the legislation in question.

On 26 January 2002, Chișinău Municipal Council issued a decision noting that the provisions of domestic legislation were contradictory in respect of the demonstrations organised by the CDPP and that the opinions of legal experts were contradictory.

In its decision of 26 January 2002, Chișinău Municipal Council stated that it had formally requested the Ministry of Justice to ask Parliament for an official and urgent interpretation of the relevant legislation.
In its decision of 26 January 2002, Chișinău Municipal Council suspended its decision of 3 January 2002 until Parliament had given its official interpretation of the relevant legislation.

In its decision of 8 February 2002, the Ministry of Justice stressed that the CDPP had breached all the laws mentioned in the decision of 18 January 2002 and that the temporary ban had been necessary and justified.
In its judgment of 17 May 2002, the Supreme Court of Justice found that since the demonstrations organised by the CDPP had been illegal, the sanction imposed on it had not been disproportionate.

In its judgment of 17 May 2002, the Supreme Court of Justice stated that in any event the Ministry of Justice's decision of 18 January 2002 had not had any negative effects on the CDPP since it had not been enforced, the CDPP's accounts had not been frozen and the party could continue its activities unhindered.
